extracted.intended_audience: aspiring periodical essayists and general writers (contributors to The Idler)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practical standards for producing short periodical essays and contributions (style, revision, novelty, submission practice) aimed at contributors to a weekly essay paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition requires slow diligence and steady perseverance
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition is, for the most part, an effort of slow diligence and steady perseverance, to which the mind is dragged by necessity or resolution, and from which the attention is every moment starting to more delightful amusements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing is usually not spontaneous delight; expect sustained effort rather than continual inspiration. Plan for incremental progress and resolve to work through distractions rather than relying on flashes of genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design vs execution: expect unexpected difficulties in execution
rubrics_metrics.description: A design which, when considered at a distance, gave flattering hopes of facility, mocks us in the execution with unexpected difficulties; the mind ... finds sometimes an unexpected barrenness and vacuity, and wonders whither all those ideas are vanished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume that an appealing outline guarantees easy drafting. Anticipate places where material will be lacking and prepare to research, invent, or restructure the project when execution falters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize scattered thoughts into method and sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes many thoughts present themselves; but so confused and unconnected, that they are not without difficulty reduced to method, or concatenated in a regular and dependent series; the mind falls at once into a labyrinth ... and toils and struggles without progress or extrication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clarity of structure: reduce abundant but unconnected ideas into a coherent order. Use outlining, ordering of dependencies, and revision to avoid a labyrinthine, unproductive draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words require as much care as ideas; diction matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Words, therefore, as well as things, claim the care of an author. ... many books might surely be produced, where just and noble sentiments are degraded and obscured by unsuitable diction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to phrasing and vocabulary deliberately; good ideas can be undermined by poor diction. Study and choose words that fit tone and content rather than assuming 'matter' will naturally find words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and patience: expect to rework near-complete passages
rubrics_metrics.description: It is one of the common distresses of a writer, to be within a word of a happy period, to want only a single epithet ... but these deficiencies cannot always be supplied: and after a long study and vexation, the passage is turned anew, and the web unwoven that was so nearly finished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to revise extensively even when a passage seems almost right. Accept that refining may require unpicking and reweaving sections; allow time for repeated edits rather than forcing a single perfect draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid self-partiality; rely on public judgment for final valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: He is still to remember, that he looks upon it with partial eyes: ... From the publick, and only from the publick, is he to await a confirmation of his claim, and a final justification of self-esteem; but the publick is not easily persuaded to favour an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the limits of self-assessment. Seek external readers and accept that public reception (subject to fashions and vocal few) ultimately determines a work's standing; beware of overvaluing one's own first impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and restraint in submissions to a periodical
rubrics_metrics.description: He excludes no style, he prohibits no subject; only let him that writes to the Idler remember, that his letters must not be long; no words are to be squandered in declarations of esteem, or confessions of inability; conscious dulness has little right to be prolix, and praise is not so welcome to the Idler as quiet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting to a periodical, be concise: avoid long-winded prefaces, insincere flattery, or unnecessary apologies. Prioritize economy of expression and respect the editor's preference for succinct contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity/secrecy about individual authorship can protect contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: The standing author of the paper is always the object of critical malignity. ... If it can be maintained, it is scarcely to be imagined at how small an expense he may grow considerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concealing which pieces are yours can diffuse critical attention and allow praise to accrue without the burden of fixed expectations. Consider anonymity or selective disclosure as a strategic choice for reputation-building in periodicals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for novelty by exploring neglected corners and fine distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: A new paper lies under the same disadvantages as a new play. ... Those that follow are forced to peep into neglected corners, to note the casual varieties of the same species, and to recommend themselves by minute industry and distinctions too subtle for common eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid repeating exhausted themes, seek overlooked subjects, small details, and subtle distinctions. Minute observation and fresh angles on familiar material are valuable sources of novelty for later writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write to entertain a broad, undemanding audience; cater to varied tastes
rubrics_metrics.description: It is naturally indifferent to this race what entertainment they receive, so they are but entertained. They catch, with equal eagerness, at a moral lecture, or the memoirs of a robber; ... the difficulty in writing is to please those from whom others learn to be pleased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a periodical aimed at 'idle' readers, prioritize variety and accessible entertainment over narrowly specialized seriousness. Balance moral, descriptive, and anecdotal pieces to match diverse reader appetites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an accessible, relatable title for a periodical
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who attempt periodical essays seem to be often stopped in the beginning, by the difficulty of finding a proper title. ... It will be easily believed of the Idler, that if his title had required any search, he never would have found it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simple, characteristic titles that signal the paper's mood or constituency rather than contrived or obscure names. A readily grasped title can better attract and identify readership.
